subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Souza <ana.souza@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Ana,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap / next steps so we have alignment on the performance SLOs and the Dedicated capacity validation you asked about:

Summary of FinTechCo targets (as I captured them):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (inference only) <= 200 ms for 512-token responses; p99 target <= 350 ms (non-streaming).
- Streaming: initial token/handshake latency < 50 ms, and steady-state per-token latency ~25-30 ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline of 50 concurrent requests (peak), with typical sustained traffic of 20 rps and bursts to 120 rps for short windows.
- Model: you mentioned wanting to validate an open LLM at 34B params with context windows up to 2k tokens.
- Reliability: graceful fallback to smaller model variant if reserved capacity hits limits; request-level retries acceptable.

What Redwood will validate during the Dedicated POC:
1) GPU sizing comparison (H100 vs A100) with the 34B model profile - per-GPU reserved throughput and headroom at your target p95/p99.
2) Concurrency tests (8, 16, 32 simultaneous streams) to measure KV cache behavior and token-rate throughput.
3) Streaming handshake + per-token latency tests to ensure start-of-stream and steady-state numbers meet your SLOs.
4) End-to-end SLO measurements inside your VPC (if Private mode) or within our Dedicated cluster (if you go with reserved capacity).

Deliverables and timing:
- Proposal & test plan (attached PDF) - includes test matrix and success criteria. I attached the preliminary sizing doc for your review.
- We can run an initial smoke test this week and a full validation next week if that timeline works for you.

Action items for FinTechCo:
- Confirm the model artifact (name & weight format) you want us to test.
- Share a small sample trace file (latency samples / typical prompt shapes) - you can send redacted examples.
- Confirm whether the POC should be within your VPC or in Dedicated on Redwood-managed infra.

I'll follow up with a proposed time window for the smoke test.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf

From: Ana Souza <ana.souza@fintechco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Aditya,

This looks right - appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- The model is finetuned-open-34B-v2 (PyTorch .pt shards). We'll provide a download link and hashes.
- Our real traffic pattern has a heavy tail of short prompts (~20 tokens) and a smaller number of long completions (~1.5k tokens). The CSV I attached shows recent latency samples under our current infra.
- For the POC we'd prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated first (faster to get started). If that looks good we may ask to move to Private VPC after.

A couple of SLO updates:
- For critical customer flows we need p95 inference <= 150 ms (tight) - if Redwood can show that on Dedicated H100 we will be more comfortable.
- For streaming chat we require start-of-stream < 40 ms for good UX on mobile.

Samir and I are available for the smoke test on Thursday (25th) between 16:00-18:00 PST.

I attached the latency samples (fintechco_latency_samples.csv) and we'll upload the model link into the Drive folder you shared.

Thanks,
Ana Souza
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
ana.souza@fintechco.com

Attachment: fintechco_latency_samples.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Souza <ana.souza@fintechco.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 14:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Ana - quick technical follow-up from the infra/serving side. Thanks for the samples, they're helpful. A few technical questions so we can craft the right test matrix:

1) Concurrency profile: when you say 50 concurrent requests, is that 50 distinct user sessions each streaming, or 50 full completions concurrently (i.e., requests that will produce 1.5k tokens)? If mixed, what's the % short vs long?
2) Tokenization: are you using a bpe tokenizer with ~0.75 tokens per word on average? We need the exact tokenizer to replicate token counts.
3) SLO enforcement: Is the p95 150 ms requirement a hard requirement for all requests, or only for the short prompt/critical flows?
4) Network constraints: do requests originate from a single region (us-west) or multi-region? We want to place Dedicated capacity accordingly.

Preliminary test plan notes (what we'll measure):
- H100 vs A100: p95/p99 at concurrency 8/16/32 for the 34B model (2k context). We expect H100 to show 20-30% better steady-state per-token throughput for 16/32 stream cases due to increased memory & better tensor cores for FP16/AMP.
- Reserved throughput: we'll provision per-GPU reserved tokens/sec (e.g., 200k tokens/minute) and measure headroom.
- Streaming handshake optimization: measure TLS + initial token generation time in your target region - aim to keep it <40 ms start-of-stream.

If you confirm the concurrency mix (percent short vs long), we'll finalize the matrix and run the smoke tests on Thu 25th 16:00 PST.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Souza <ana.souza@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps

Ana/Samir - thanks for confirming the slot. A couple of quick notes and proposed test plan (high level):

1) Concurrency mix: please confirm but we'll assume for the smoke test a 70/30 split (70% short prompts ~20 tokens, 30% long completions ~1.5k tokens). If you can confirm or update that ratio before 15:00 PST today that would be ideal.

2) GPU plan: we'll run back-to-back tests on H100 and A100 instances in the Dedicated cluster. Test runs:
   - Warm-up + baseline: single-stream 512-token runs to collect cold vs warm cache numbers.
   - Concurrency sweep: 8, 16, 32 concurrent streams (mixed 70/30) measuring p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/sec.
   - Streaming latency: handshake + first-token + per-token steady-state for a 1.5k completion streamed back to the client.

3) Reserved throughput: we'll propose reserving X GPUs to match your 50 concurrent requests target and show the margin for bursts (we'll provide a per-GPU throughput number after the baseline).

4) Success criteria for the POC:
   - H100: show p95 <= 150 ms for short prompts and start-of-stream <= 40 ms for streaming in the us-west region.
   - If H100 meets criteria and A100 is within 20% of the target, we will include both as options in the sizing doc.

I've uploaded the final sizing proposal to the Drive link and attached a PDF here. Rafael will run the test jobs and will share raw metrics + plot outputs after each run.

See you at 16:00 PST.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf

From: Ana Souza <ana.souza@fintechco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks team - confirmed. 70/30 mix is correct for the POC. We'll make the model artifacts available in the Drive folder and Samir will be on the call at 16:00 PST.

Small ask: if you can also include p99 numbers in the post-test report (we need to see tail behavior) that would be great.

Looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Ana
